nodes.name: Fetch 8-Ks
nodes.notes: Deliberately does NOT send &items=. That parameter is served through an edge cache whose key sometimes omits it, returning another query result with HTTP 200. Items are filtered client-side downstream.

nodes.name: Filter Item Codes
nodes.notes: The trap-proof half. items[] arrives on every hit, so the day is filtered here rather than by the server.

nodes.name: Upsert Catalysts
nodes.notes: Idempotent on (accession, item_code). Re-running a day updates in place instead of duplicating.

nodes.name: Plan Time Enrichment
nodes.notes: Full-text search only carries a file DATE. Exact acceptance time comes from the per-company submissions API, fetched only for earnings and deduped by CIK.

nodes.name: Fetch Filing Times
nodes.notes: Batched to stay far inside SEC 10 req/sec. One company failing must not lose the sweep.

nodes.notes: Observability only. No model call anywhere in this workflow, so no spend check is required.

parameters.content:
## The trap this avoids

SEC full-text search accepts `&items=2.02`, but an edge cache in front of `efts.sec.gov` sometimes drops that key and serves a **different query result with HTTP 200 and no error**. Recon caught it when eight rapid queries across unrelated item codes all returned the same count.

This workflow fetches the whole day and filters `_source.items` in code. Two to four requests instead of one, and deterministic.

## Cost and keys

**No API key. No account. No registration.** SEC allows scripted access at 10 req/sec with a declared User-Agent.

Per run: 2-8 requests for the sweep, plus one per earnings company for the exact acceptance time.

**No model call happens here** - 8-K item codes are structured data, so scoring and classification are a deterministic lookup table. Nothing to meter.
